rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken construction for considering A to be B.

example.english: We regard him as one of our own.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 dong1 keoi5 hai6 zi6 gei2 jan4

rows.note: Use this formal or written verb when describing A as B in more elevated language.

example.english: We regard this document as a formal contract.
example.traditional: 我哋視呢份文件為正式合約。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 si6 ni1 fan6 man4 gin6 wai4 zing3 sik1 hap6 joek3

rows.note: Use 方面 as the all-purpose noun for an aspect or an 'in this regard' reference.

example.english: I’ll talk to you more with regard to this aspect.
example.jyutping: ni1 fong1 min6 ngo5 wui5 zoi3 tung4 nei5 king1

rows.note: Use this construction for regard as personal concern or care for another person, not for relation or reference.

example.english: My regard for Mum is not just about buying things for her.
example.traditional: 我對阿媽嘅關心，唔係淨係買嘢畀佢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 deoi3 aa3 maa1 ge3 gwaan1 sam1 m4 hai6 zing6 hai6 maai5 je5 bei2 keoi5

rows.note: Use 目光 for a steady look or gaze rather than an eye expression such as 眼神.

example.english: Their regard stayed fixed on me.
example.traditional: 佢嘅目光一直停留喺我身上。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ge3 muk6 gwong1 jat1 zik6 ting4 lau4 hai2 ngo5 san1 soeng6

rows.note: Use this noun phrase when regard means the respect or esteem shown toward someone or something.

example.english: Everyone can see our regard for the teacher.
example.traditional: 大家都睇得出我哋對老師嘅尊重。
example.jyutping: daai6 gaa1 dou1 tai2 dak1 ceot1 ngo5 dei6 deoi3 lou5 si1 ge3 zyun1 zung6
